title: Cross-Dataset Generalization of Underwater Acoustic Ship Recognition: A Four-Dataset Benchmark of Label and Acoustic Domain Shifts
content: Deep networks for underwater acoustic target recognition (UATR) are almost always trained and evaluated on a single dataset, leaving cross-dataset generalization unmeasured. We benchmark four ship-radiated-noise datasets—Strait-of-Georgia marine Oceanship, freshwater-lake QiandaoEar22, an AIS-auto-labeled VTUAD reconstruction from public Ocean Networks Canada archives, and nearshore-harbor ShipsEar—under one preprocessing chain and frozen recording/clip-level splits. The classifiers are ImageNet-pretrained ResNet-18. Within the operationally comparable label space defined by our mapping tables (18.5%, 22.4%, 13.3%, and 56.4% of the four test sets, respectively), direct transfer degrades severely in all twelve cross-dataset directions: accuracies of 0.0–47.9% fall well below the majority-class baselines of 55.6–88.9% of the corresponding evaluated subsets. This conclusion is supported jointly by accuracy, macro-F1, per-class recall, mapped-subset coverage, and unmapped-prediction analyses; isolated class-level signals do not yield a usable cross-dataset operating point. The same-region Oceanship→VTUAD pair reaches only 0.9% with the tuned checkpoint and 2.9% with the sqrt-weighted checkpoint (Section 3.4), indicating that water-body differences alone are not sufficient to explain the observed transfer failure; differences in labeling provenance, scenario construction, sensor configuration, vessel population, and temporal sampling remain plausible contributing factors. Centroid-level analysis shows the cross-dataset gap is 5–17 times the within-dataset inter-class distance. Under Oceanship’s 4,278:1 imbalance, sqrt-smoothed class weights raise macro-F1 from 0.1302 to 0.1452, whereas naive inverse weighting destabilizes training. The mapping tables, frozen splits, and evaluation code are released at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22906116 as a reproducible cross-dataset UATR benchmark.
